claim: Red Hat OpenShift AI exposes llm-d's router as a single 'router' field on the LLMInferenceService CRD with route, gateway, and scheduler sub-fields, which can be left empty to use operator-managed defaults.
stance_target: downstream products embed llm-d's router by wrapping it in a higher-level CRD rather than reimplementing scheduling logic
scope_conditions: Red Hat OpenShift AI 3.4, LLMInferenceService serving.kserve.io/v1alpha1

claim: The EPP is built on the Kubernetes SIG Gateway API Inference Extension and integrates with standard gateways (Istio, Envoy Gateway) via the ext-proc protocol, making it portable across gateway implementations.
stance_target: EPP's integration boundary with the data plane is the ext-proc gRPC protocol, not a k8s-specific API
quoted_support: The EPP is built on Gateway API Inference Extension, a Kubernetes SIG project. It works with standard gateways like Istio or Envoy Gateway through the ext-proc protocol, so it plugs into infrastructure you may already have.

claim: Upstream llm-d benchmarks on shared-prefix workloads show TTFT dropping from 35 seconds to 120 milliseconds (>99% reduction) and throughput increasing 151% on 8 vLLM replicas across 16 H100 GPUs (Qwen3-32B, 60 RPS).
stance_target: KV-cache-aware EPP routing delivers large, reproducible gains over standard Kubernetes Service routing
scope_conditions: 8 vLLM replicas, 16 H100 GPUs (TP=2), Qwen3-32B, shared-prefix synthetic workload, 60 RPS
quoted_support: Time-to-first-token: 35 seconds to 120 milliseconds. Prefix cache hits skip the expensive prefill entirely (more than 99% reduction). Throughput: More than doubled (+151%).

claim: The EPP's default prefix-cache tracking is self-referential (it hashes and remembers its own past routing decisions) rather than introspecting vLLM engines directly; a 'precise prefix cache mode' that reads actual KV cache entries is optional today but expected to become default in a future release.
stance_target: distinction between approximate and precise prefix-cache tracking modes in the EPP
scope_conditions: llm-d EPP default profile as of mid-2026
quoted_support: By default, the EPP tracks its own routing decisions: it hashes incoming prompts into blocks and compares them against what it has previously routed to each pod... For workloads with high cache churn, llm-d also offers a precise prefix cache mode that introspects each vLLM instance for actual KV cache entries. Precise mode is expected to become the default in a future release.

claim: llm-d's predicted-latency scheduling uses an XGBoost model trained on live traffic with roughly 5% mean absolute percentage error (MAPE), allowing requests to carry SLO headers like x-slo-ttft-ms.
stance_target: llm-d supports SLO-driven predictive scheduling beyond simple cache/queue scoring
quoted_support: An XGBoost model trained on live traffic predicts per-pod time-to-first-token (TTFT) and time-per-output-token (about 5% mean absolute percentage error (MAPE)). Requests can include service level objective (SLO) headers like x-slo-ttft-ms to route against latency targets.
